note: T-3334. The light people made on Prairie Avenue in 1904, drawn when Settings › Time of day darkens it (renderers/web/js/night-lights.js). Every house's window panes can glow, building by building, as share_by_hour says; the colour is between a gas mantle's and an early electric lamp's, warmer than daylight and whiter than a candle. The street lamps are lit by street-furniture.js from the T-3199 posts. Liberty L-night-lights-3334 records what is ours.

windows.basis: Gas mantles, 'producing brighter light with only one-twelfth the gas consumption, became available in the 1890s', the city 'still used gas streetlights in some areas' into the early 1900s, and 'Electric lights were common by 1909' (chipublib_gaslight_blog). Light no longer cost a candle an hour, so the houses are lit more and later than 1835's town. Which houses burned gas and which electricity, and the hours, are ours.
